models.name: discussionboard_notifications
models.description:
Notification delivery record - This implements the notification delivery and tracking requirements from the requirements document (cf. notification mechanisms in core functional requirements and audit requirements). 

Business purpose: Keeps a persistent, queryable record of every notification (on-site, push, or email) sent to members concerning discussion board updates, replies, moderation outcomes, mentions, and critical policy changes. Ensures members can review notification history, supports audit/compliance logging, and allows for notification status management (delivered/read).

Normalization: 3NF compliant; notifications are only related to actual events (referenced by IDs), with no redundant/cached values. For example, a notification for a new moderator action would reference the related content without duplicating post/comment content here.

Key relationships: Will have a foreign key to discussionboard_members (member receiving the notification), and potentially to referenced entities (posts, comments, reports) via their IDs if required—those are soft-foreigns (UUIDs) to allow referencing dynamic business objects.

Special behaviors: Notifications are immutable records—once sent, status can only be updated (delivered/read), content doesn't change. Used for compliance/audit event trails.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies the notification delivery record.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: Target member's {@link discussionboard_members.id} who is receiving this notification. Ensures referential integrity between notification targets and registered users.

plainFields.name: type
plainFields.description: Type of the notification (e.g., reply, mention, moderation_outcome, warning, policy_update, etc.). Implements requirement for notification categorization by event type. Ensures members can distinguish between notification classes. 3NF compliant by avoiding event duplication.

plainFields.name: entity_type
plainFields.description: Kind of entity this notification references (e.g., post, comment, report, appeal, thread, policy). Implements requirement for referencing specific board objects related to the notification. Keeps this data atomic per 3NF.

plainFields.name: entity_id
plainFields.description: ID of the business object this notification refers to (e.g., ID of a post, comment, report, etc.). Implements cross-entity traceability. Normalized: only contains object reference, not embedded content.

plainFields.name: message
plainFields.description: Notification message shown to member (short body). Implements business requirement for delivering readable notification content. Normalization: message is tailored for notification but not duplicate of any business content.

plainFields.name: delivered_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when notification was delivered. 3NF: atomic business fact. Used for audit trail and delivery status UI.

plainFields.name: read_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when notification was marked as read by the member. Null if unread. Implements read-status tracking per user, normalized to this entity (not duplicated elsewhere).

plainFields.name: channel
plainFields.description: Delivery channel (on_site, email, push, sms, etc). Implements requirement for specifying how notification was sent. Ensures UI can offer opt-out and channel-based filtering. Normalization: atomic value per record.

models.name: discussionboard_notification_preferences
models.description:
Notification preference settings for each member - This implements the requirement to allow members to configure how and for which events they receive notifications, as described in notification mechanism requirements.

Business purpose: Allows every member to store their notification preferences per notification type and channel (e.g., receive new reply notifications via on-site only, moderate actions by email, mentions by both, etc). Preferences drive notification delivery logic (e.g., block sending if opted out).

Normalization: 3NF compliance achieved by atomically storing each event type and channel in a preference row, rather than as a denormalized map or structure. For example, storing (member, type, channel, enabled) uniquely for every preference instead of an array keeps redundant data out.

Key relationships: Each record references the member (discussionboard_members table) whose preference is configured.

Special behaviors: Application logic ensures that on account deletion, all preferences are removed. Changes here directly affect notification sending at runtime.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies the preference row.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_member_id
foreignFields.description: {@link discussionboard_members.id} of the user whose preferences are being saved. Implements per-user notification customization, as required by the notification delivery and opt-out system. Maintains referential integrity with the member registry.

plainFields.name: type
plainFields.description: Notification type this preference relates to (e.g., reply, mention, moderation_outcome, warning). Implements the event-based preference logic required. Atomic value per 3NF; ensures each row configures exactly one type.

plainFields.name: channel
plainFields.description: The delivery channel for this preference ('on_site', 'email', 'push', etc). Implements the requirement for channel-based opt-out and customization. Atomic and 3NF normalized.

plainFields.name: enabled
plainFields.description: Whether this member wants to receive this type of notification via this channel. Implements the opt-in/opt-out business requirement for notification personalization. No denormalized/cached flag map, 3NF compliant.

models.name: discussionboard_search_indexes
models.description:
Discussion board search index - This implements the search acceleration and full-text search requirement from the requirements document (see discussionboard_core_functional_requirements.md section 6: 'Search, Tagging, & Discovery').

Business purpose: Facilitates fast retrieval of posts, comments, and associated data for keyword and metadata-based searches, essential for performant user-facing discovery features. This table maintains a normalized, query-efficient structure for the inverted index or summary of searchable entities. Maintains 3NF compliance by separating search optimization data from the main content tables, with all index records strictly referencing the original content by unique identifiers. 

Usage example: Used when a user searches for keywords, tags, or authors; powers autocomplete, relevance scoring, and result ranking systems.

Key relationships: Reference to target entities such as posts, comments, threads (by their uuid), and tracking type. No foreign keys in this domain—relations are unidirectional from index towards existing business tables in other components. 

Special behaviors: Only core normalized index metadata is stored here—no computed ranking or denormalized result summaries allowed (those may be materialized in reporting views if necessary).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each search index record.

foreignFields.name: entity_id
foreignFields.description: Target entity's {@link discussionboard_posts.id}, {@link discussionboard_comments.id}, or other content UUID depending on entity_type.

plainFields.name: entity_type
plainFields.description: Type of entity referenced by this index record - Implements requirement for polymorphic search indexation (e.g., 'post', 'comment', 'thread'). Ensures normalization by recording only the primary entity type in atomic string format. For example, value 'post' for indexing a post content.

plainFields.name: indexed_text
plainFields.description: Aggregated and normalized text used for full-text search - Combines title, body, and metadata fields in a canonical order for indexing. Implements core search requirements (requirement section 6). Stays fully normalized by representing only the atomic, canonical string. For example, concatenated post title and content, or comment body.

plainFields.name: indexed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this index entry was last generated/updated - Implements search freshness and incremental indexing needs. Maintains normalization by being a single timestamp per record. For example, updated whenever the associated entity changes.

models.name: discussionboard_search_histories
models.description:
Discussion board search histories - This implements the search analytics, audit, and user engagement/tracking requirements (see requirements 'audit & compliance logging' and 'search, tagging & discovery').

Business purpose: Records members' search actions, including terms searched and contextual metadata for system learning, personalization, and auditing. Maintains 3NF compliance by recording only normalized, atomic search event data. No aggregations or user-calculated fields present.

Usage example: Used for features like recent search re-surfacing, search analytics, and transparency/audit reporting.

Key relationships: Optionally references the member performing the search, and records search parameters and timestamps. No direct foreign keys in this table for loose coupling, but 'member_id' is provided as a reference for personalization/audit (references discussionboard_members.id).

Special behaviors: All data fully normalized; denormalized or aggregated reports must be built in separate materialized views.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each search history event.

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to search-performing member's {@link discussionboard_members.id} - Implements user-specific audit and personalization requirements. No enforced FK constraint for privacy and audit integrity.

plainFields.name: search_terms
plainFields.description: Raw search query string(s) executed in this event - Implements the requirement for search auditing and analytics. Records the user's exact input, fully normalized as an atomic value per search event.

plainFields.name: search_filters
plainFields.description: Serialized search filters or metadata (e.g., tags, date ranges) - Implements search capability analytics; records in atomic (normalized) format only, never as precomputed lists or aggregates. Example: JSON or CSV with filter parameters.

plainFields.name: performed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this search was performed - Required by audit, analytics, and for supporting 'recent searches' features. 3NF compliance: single value per row, no rollup.

plainFields.name: result_count
plainFields.description: Number of results returned for this search event - Implements analytics requirement for search effectiveness, normalized with one row per search event. (May be used for user feedback and reporting.)

models.name: discussionboard_policies
models.description: Platform Policy Record - Implements the core platform policy requirements, giving a canonical, versioned record for all operational and behavioral policy rules. Policy data is strictly normalized and auditable, directly mapping to documentation requirements and board policy enforcement. Example: 'Community Guidelines v2.3' issued on a specific date. Integrates with audit logs and is referenced for compliance and moderator review. Only most recent is currently enforced, older remain for trace/audit.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each discussion board policy record.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Policy title, e.g. 'Community Guidelines' or 'Content Moderation Policy'. Maintains normalization, avoids duplication. Implements document clarity.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Full text body of the policy, in markdown or rich text. Implements requirement for accessible, canonical platform policy. For example, the text visible to all members or in legal export. Fully normalized: not duplicated in reports/notifications.

plainFields.name: version
plainFields.description: Version or revision string, e.g. 'v2.3'. Tracks updates and historic changes. Enables transparent history/audit. Example: used for date-based policy lookup or regulatory export.

plainFields.name: effective_at
plainFields.description: The date/time when the policy comes into effect. Enables lifecycle and audit tracing. Null when not yet active or for drafts. For example: a policy published for enforcement starting next month.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: When a policy is superseded or withdrawn. Null if still current. Ensures that only one policy is enforced at a time and supports regulatory retention requirements.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of policy creation. Satisfies requirements for audit logging.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last update. Ensures audit and policy lifecycle are tracked.

plainFields.name: created_by
plainFields.description: UUID of the member/moderator/admin who created this policy. Supports audit reporting, foreign key to actors table (exists in other component). Does not duplicate actor data.

models.name: discussionboard_policy_updates
models.description: Policy Update/Event Log - Implements transparent policy change and notification history. Records all updates to policies, enabling complete audit/compliance trail. Mapped directly to board transparency, legal, and user-notification requirements. Allows admins/moderators/members to see what was changed, when, and by whom. Enforces 3NF by separating update events/actors from the policy content itself.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each policy update record.

foreignFields.name: discussionboard_policy_id
foreignFields.description: Target policy being updated. References {@link discussionboard_policies.id}, supporting referential integrity. Key in policy-update history. Maintains normalization in event/audit trails.

foreignFields.name: actor_id

plainFields.name: change_summary
plainFields.description: Summary description of what changed and why (for transparency and audit); e.g., 'Clarified spam definition; updated reporting workflow.' 3NF compliance: not embedded in policy or notification structures.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Event creation timestamp. Satisfies need for sequenced, auditable event logs.

models.name: discussionboard_community_guidelines
models.description: Community Guidelines Canonical Record - Fulfills the need for a canonical, structured storage of community guidelines, versioned with independent lifecycle tracking. Integrates with moderation and onboarding functions. Ensures canonical, up-to-date guidelines are referenceable without duplication. Only currently effective guideline is visible to members; previous versions are preserved for legal and compliance review.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for community guidelines.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Guideline section or doc title, e.g. 'Acceptable Use', 'Prohibited Behavior'. Atomic/normalized for search/display.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Full guideline content, markdown allowed. Canonical, structural, normalized; covers the specific rules detailed for users/moderators/auditors.

plainFields.name: version
plainFields.description: Version/revision tag, e.g. 'v2.0', '2025-07'. Enables traceable guideline life cycle. Normalized: not duplicated in child records.

plainFields.name: effective_at

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when guideline section is created. Audit log compliance and historical integrity.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last change to guideline text. Complete update/audit trail. 3NF: kept atomic to avoid duplicate history.

## Systematic

```mermaid
"discussionboard_sections" }o--|| "discussionboard_channels" : section_channel
"discussionboard_settings" }o--o| "discussionboard_sections" : settings_section
```

### `discussionboard_channels`

Discussion Board Channels - Implements the system's multi-board partitioning requirement from the introduction and purpose documentation.

This model represents distinct logical channels within the overall discussion platform, each potentially covering a broad topic area or serving as an umbrella for more granular discussion boards. Each channel groups related sections or boards, allowing for flexible configuration, discoverability, and moderation boundaries.

Maintains 3NF by storing only channel-specific atomic data. For example, a platform could have channels such as 'Politics', 'Economics', each of which houses multiple sub-boards or sections.

Key relationships: Referenced by sections and boards for hierarchical organization.
Special behaviors: Supports soft deletion for audit trail, and can be toggled as visible or hidden in global navigation.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each discussion channel.
- `name`: Channel name - Implements the naming structure requirement for top-level forum partitioning. Stores a unique, human-readable identifier for this channel (e.g., 'Politics', 'Economics'). Ensures normalization by separating channel name from any derived or display content. For example, 'International Affairs'.
- `description`: Channel description - Implements the metadata/context requirement. Provides a brief explanation of what the channel covers, aiding user navigation and discoverability. Maintains normalization by not mixing this with posts or boards' content. For example, 'Debate topics on domestic and world politics.'.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp - Implements the audit/compliance requirement. Records when the channel was established. For example, '2023-11-21T14:00:00Z'.
- `updated_at`: Update timestamp - Audit/compliance requirement; indicates the last time channel info was modified. Enables efficient auditing and change detection.
- `deleted_at`: Deletion timestamp (for soft-delete) - Enables reversible/historical auditing per policy requirements. Null if not deleted. Ensures normalization by not removing records outright. For example, '2024-01-01T09:00:00Z' or null.
- `is_visible`: Visibility flag - Implements platform-wide configuration requirement. If false, channel is hidden from general navigation. Ensures atomic control over channel's appearance. For example, false when shutting down a channel for policy reasons.

### `discussionboard_sections`

Discussion Board Sections - Implements the hierarchical board structure requirement from the introduction and purpose and organizational requirements.

Each section represents a further subdivision within a channel, typically covering a subtopic or grouping related boards. Normalized to contain only atomic section-level data. Used to organize boards and topics for intuitive navigation and delegated moderation.

For example, the 'Economics' channel may contain the sections 'Macroeconomics', 'Microeconomics', and 'Policy'.

Key relationships: Contains a foreign key reference to its parent channel. Referenced by boards for sectional grouping.
Special behaviors: Supports position ordering for display, and soft deletion for recoverability.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each discussion section.
- `discussionboard_channel_id`: Parent channel's [discussionboard_channels.id](#discussionboard_channels). Establishes the section's top-level grouping for platform navigation and moderation boundaries.
- `name`: Section name - Implements the requirement for sub-board labeling. Human-readable label for the section (e.g., 'Macroeconomics'). Distinct per channel. Maintains normalization by separating label from display or content data.
- `description`: Section description - Supports metadata/context requirements. Provides additional information about the section's focus. Kept nullable for brevity or when not required by policy. For example, 'All discussions related to global economic trends.'
- `position`: Section ordering position - Implements display order requirements for UI. Stored as an integer; allows reordering without changing IDs.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp - For audit/compliance tracking. Records the date/time the section was created.
- `updated_at`: Update timestamp - Last modification to section metadata. For change detection and audit trails.
- `deleted_at`: Soft-deletion timestamp. Null if not deleted, otherwise indicates when section was hidden for policy/compliance purposes.
- `is_visible`: Visibility flag - Determines if section is displayed in navigation/search. Set false to temporarily hide. Implements atomic access and policy toggling requirement.

### `discussionboard_configurations`

System Configuration Registry - Implements the platform-wide settings/audit requirements.

Contains all global key-value configuration entries for the discussion board system (e.g., maintenance mode, password policy, default board behaviors). Fully normalized to ensure each config setting is atomic. Business logic implementation reads keys/values for runtime system behavior.

Key relationships: No foreign keys—self-contained for architectural separation.
Special behaviors: Supports type safety enforcement and versioned auditing.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each configuration record.
- `config_key`: Configuration key - Implements requirement for named config registry entries; e.g., 'maintenance_mode', 'max_post_length'. Ensures each config parameter is individually addressable. Unique for the schema.
- `config_value`: Configuration value - Stores actual config data, always as a string for normalization across boolean, numeric, text settings. For example: 'true', '2048', 'Welcome to the board!'.
- `value_type`: Value type - Implements explicit type tracking requirement; e.g., 'boolean', 'int', 'string', 'datetime'. Separates data from type for normalization and safety.
- `description`: Config description - Documents the purpose/usage of each config; assists admins and devs. For example, 'Enables or disables new user signups.'. Not shown to regular members.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp for the configuration entry. Supports auditing and compliance logging.
- `updated_at`: Last updated timestamp for the entry. Aids in config change tracking.

### `discussionboard_audit_logs`

System Audit Log - Implements the audit/compliance logging requirement.

Stores all significant system-level and user-led actions related to policy enforcement, administrative changes, and moderation outcomes, as required by operational and regulatory guidelines. Keeps normalized, atomic records for actions, actors, and metadata. Used for retrospective investigations, compliance audits, and appeals analysis.

Key relationships: Optionally references member/admin records in Actors component for actor_id.
Special behaviors: NEVER soft-delete; logs are permanent as required by compliance. Large volume/readonly design for performance.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each audit log record.
- `actor_id`: Optional reference to actor (member/moderator/admin) who performed the action. Links to discussionboard_members, discussionboard_moderators, or discussionboard_admins in Actors component. Null for system or anonymous events. Ensures normalization by referencing, never storing actor names.
- `action_type`: Type of action logged (e.g., 'POST_EDIT', 'USER_BAN', 'CONFIG_UPDATE', 'REPORT_ESCALATE'). Implements detailed event catalog for traceability. Normalized string values.
- `action_scope`: Scope of the affected resource (e.g., 'post', 'comment', 'user', 'system'). Supports multi-entity audit coverage. Maintains normalization by not embedding resource details here.
- `target_id`: ID of the affected resource (may refer to post, comment, config, etc. Schema-enforced by scope and audit logic). Atomic, polymorphic reference. Null if not applicable (e.g., system-level events).
- `metadata`: Optional additional context/parameters for this log entry in serialized (e.g., JSON) format. For example, change diff, before/after values. Maintains normalization by never duplicating structural data. Kept as string for DB-agnosticism.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp for the audit log event. Immutable; required for all entries. Forms the timeline basis for compliance reporting.

### `discussionboard_settings`

Lightweight System Settings - Implements per-section or user-overrideable parameters for the platform.

Configured as a separate table from configurations for localized, frequently-overridden, or member-facing settings (e.g., default notification preferences, custom display toggles). Normalized to link each setting either globally or to a logical owner (e.g., section, member).

Key relationships: May reference sections, members, or be system-global.
Special behaviors: Settings can be inherited or overridden per the type/owner.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each settings record.
- `section_id`: Optional reference to a section ([discussionboard_sections.id](#discussionboard_sections)) for section-level settings. Null for global/system settings. Ensures normalization by not repeating setting values per section without context.
- `setting_key`: Settings key - Unique identifier for this parameter; e.g., 'default_sort', 'theme_mode'. Implements settings registry requirement; atomic per entry.
- `setting_value`: Settings value - String representation of the current setting. Maintains normalization without mixing with configuration data.
- `owner_type`: Owner type - Implements scope-separation requirement. Defines if this setting is global, per-section, or per-member; e.g., 'global', 'section', 'member'. Required for scope enforcement.
- `owner_id`: Optional reference to a board member or other owner. Null for global or section-scoped settings. Normalized for privacy and audit reasons.
- `description`: Detailed description of this setting, for admin UI or developer documentation. Not displayed to general members. For example, 'Sets the default sort order for new posts in this section.'
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the setting entry was created. Required for audit and configuration traceability.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp for last modification to this record. Aids auditing and change notifications.

### `discussionboard_members`

Discussion Board Member Entity - Implements the user/member business entity requirement for the Actors domain.

This model stores registered user accounts who can participate in posts and comments, report content, and manage their profile. Maintains strict 3NF normalization: profile data, role assignments, and history are separated into respective tables. For example, the 'discussionboard_member_profiles' entity links here by foreign key for extended details.

Key relationships: one-to-one/optional with discussionboard_member_profiles, one-to-many with discussionboard_member_histories, and references to role assignment tables. Core for authentication and authorization.
Special behaviors: Email must be unique, username must be unique within the platform, soft deletion supported.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the discussion board member.
- `email`: Member's email address - Implements user identification and notification requirements. Used for login and notification triggers. Ensures 3NF: not duplicated elsewhere. For example, 'jane.doe@example.com'. Unique constraint enforced.
- `username`: Unique username chosen by the member - Implements the requirement for member identity display and mention system. Not null, unique within system. For example, 'policy_watcher'.
- `password_hash`: Hashed password for secure authentication - Directly maps authentication requirement. Enforces normalization: hash stored here only. Value is not the plaintext password. For example, a bcrypt hash string.
- `created_at`: Datetime of account creation - Required for audit trail. Used in user onboarding and compliance logging. Always set at account creation. For example, 2024-07-22T15:15:48+09:00.
- `updated_at`: Datetime of the most recent update to the member record. Tracks profile/account changes per audit requirements. Updated on any change to member data.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp - Implements platform's right to erasure and retention policy. Null if not deleted; set to deletion time if deleted.

### `discussionboard_moderators`

Discussion Board Moderator Assignment Entity - Implements the role assignment requirement for moderators. 

This model records which members are assigned moderator rights. Each row represents a member with granted moderator privileges, enforcing permission control and auditability per requirements in 02_discussionboard_user_roles_and_journeys.md. Maintains 3NF by referencing members via foreign key.

Key relationships: FK to discussionboard_members (each moderator is a member), log of when and by whom the privilege was granted. Used for authorization checks and auditing moderation actions.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for moderator assignment.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) who is assigned as moderator. Fulfills moderator assignment requirement.
- `granted_by_admin_id`: Admin's [discussionboard_admins.id](#discussionboard_admins) who granted moderator rights. Fulfills the admin-controlled assignment or revocation of moderator status.
- `granted_at`: Datetime when moderator rights were assigned. Required for audit and permission review. For example, 2024-07-22T15:15:48+09:00.
- `revoked_at`: Datetime moderator rights were revoked (if applicable). Required for tracking ongoing and former moderators. Null if currently moderator.

### `discussionboard_admins`

Discussion Board Admin Entity - Implements admin account business requirement for the Actors domain.

Stores system-level platform administrators with permissions to manage users, moderators, board configuration, and compliance. Maintains 3NF by separating admin core data from member entity. Used for assignment of roles, escalation handling, platform oversight.

Key relationships: can be referenced by discussionboard_moderators (as grantor), and linked to audit logs/history for actions.
Special behaviors: Unique email per admin, and activity audit trail.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the discussion board admin.
- `email`: Admin's email address. Implements requirement for admin authentication and notification. Unique among administrators. For example, 'admin@platform.com'.
- `username`: Admin username for system login and identification. Implements requirement for admin actions attribution. Unique, non-null within admins only. For example, 'supermod'.
- `password_hash`: Hashed password for admin secure authentication. Implements authentication and audit requirements. Value is not plaintext password.
- `created_at`: Datetime of admin account creation. Required for onboarding audit and compliance logging.
- `updated_at`: Datetime of latest admin profile/account update. For precise audit trail per 3NF.
- `deleted_at`: Datetime admin account was soft deleted. Null if current; set if removed per retention policy.

### `discussionboard_member_profiles`

Discussion Board Member Profile Entity - Implements the member profile extension requirement from 02_discussionboard_user_roles_and_journeys.md.

Stores extended profile information (display name, bio, preferences) for each member, separated for normalization and privacy. Maintains strict 3NF; profile details are not stored in core member entity. For example, allows null bio for new accounts, or diverse locales. Used to enrich user experience and for search/discovery features.

Key relationships: Each profile is tied to a member by 1:1 FK; referenced for displaying user info on posts and comments. Profile can be updated separately from account.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for member profile.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: FK to [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) - the member whose profile this is. Implements 1:1 mapping between member and profile.
- `display_name`: Display name visible on posts/comments. Implements requirement for user-facing identification separate from username. Nullable to support privacy settings.
- `bio`: Profile bio or introduction text. Implements enrich profile/expression requirement. Nullable for members who do not provide a bio.
- `avatar_url`: Public avatar image link for the member profile. Separate from core account for normalization. Nullable for users without avatars.
- `locale`: ISO code for user's UI language/locale setting. For internationalization. Nullable.
- `timezone`: User's preferred timezone (IANA tz format, e.g., "Asia/Seoul"). Supports correct timestamp conversion for notifications. Nullable.
- `created_at`: Datetime when the profile was created. Required for audit trail and compliance.
- `updated_at`: Last profile update time. Tracks modifications, used for search/sorting features.

### `discussionboard_member_histories`

Member History Change/Audit Entity - Implements compliance, audit trail, and profile change history requirements.

Tracks all significant changes for each member: profile updates, role changes, suspensions, and other actions. Supports platform audit, allows admin to review history. Maintains 3NF by referencing the affected member by FK with no redundant data.

Key relationships: many-to-one with discussionboard_members (each member has multiple history entries), referenced during compliance reviews.
Special behaviors: History is immutable; original event data is always preserved.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for member history record.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: FK to [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) - the member whose change history is recorded. Implements requirement for cross-entity audit trails.
- `change_type`: Type of change (e.g., 'profile_update', 'role_granted', 'suspended'). Implements requirement for event categorization and review. Normalized: not repeated elsewhere.
- `change_data`: JSON-encoded structured details about the change - Implements additional context for the history event. For example, old/new values in a profile update. Supports audit compliance.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the history entry was created (i.e., when the action occurred). For audit trail and compliance.

### `discussionboard_boards`

Board entity - This implements the requirement for organizing discussions by separate boards (see requirements: Introduction, Service Scope, and Core Functional Requirements on board-level categorization). 

Business explanation: Represents a dedicated board (such as 'General Politics', 'Economics', 'International Affairs') to group threads according to subject or purpose. Supports separation of discussion topics and board-level access control, moderation, and configuration.
Maintains 3NF compliance by isolating board attributes from threads/posts. For example, a new 'Elections 2025' board can be created without modifying thread or post tables.

Key relationships: Will be referenced by thread, post, and moderation policy models in other domains/files. 
Special behaviors: Board can be activated/deactivated, may contain links to policies or display features.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each board entity.
- `name`: Board name - Implements the board labeling requirement. Human-readable title for the board, e.g., 'Global Economy'. Enforces normalization by being atomic (1NF). Example: Shown at top of board view.
- `description`: Board description - Implements the requirement for clear labeling and explanation of purpose. Supplies a summary that users see when browsing available boards. Ensures normalization as a direct attribute. Example: 'Discuss world economic trends and data.'
- `is_active`: Whether the board is currently active/visible. Implements access control requirement. Directly managed by admins. Example: Board may be deactivated during policy reviews.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp - Implements audit logging requirement. Records when the board was established. Ensures integrity for audit purposes. Example: Used in admin logs.
- `updated_at`: Last updated timestamp for the board (implements audit & compliance requirements). Updated any time board configuration changes. Example: Tracks admin updates to board settings.

### `discussionboard_board_tags`

Board-level tag entity - Implements the tag taxonomy management requirement for boards (see requirements: Core Functional Requirements, Tagging & Discovery section). 

Business explanation: Allows boards to be associated with predefined or user-curated tags for improved sorting, searchability, and discovery. Maintains normalized tag assignments; tags may be used for search, recommendations, or access filtering.
3NF compliance is maintained by isolating tag data from boards and other entities.

Key relationships: Will reference discussionboard_boards (via foreign key). May be referenced by search/index systems. 
Special behaviors: Duplicate tag names per board are prevented by composite unique constraint.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each board tag entry.
- `discussionboard_board_id`: Referenced board's [discussionboard_boards.id](#discussionboard_boards) - links tag to a specific board. Supports 1:N assignment of tags to boards.
- `tag`: The tag value (e.g., 'Policy', 'Debate') assigned to this board. Implements tag requirement for cross-board discovery and sorting. Example: Used as filter in board search lists. Normalization: atomic and unique within board context.
- `created_at`: When this tag was created or assigned to the board. Implements audit and compliance traceability. For example, supports querying recent tag additions.

### `discussionboard_board_categories`

Board categorization entity - Implements the requirement for supporting hierarchical or topical categorization of boards (see: Service Scope and Tagging/Discovery requirements). 

Business explanation: Allows admins to group boards under broader categories (such as 'Politics', 'Economics', 'Society'), enabling multi-board discovery, filtering, and reporting. Maintains 3NF: category metadata is not duplicated within boards.

Key relationships: Referenced by boards (each board can reference a category), and by reporting modules.
Special behaviors: Category names must be globally unique. 

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for board category.
- `name`: The display name for the category (e.g., 'Economics', 'Global Affairs'). Implements category organization. Normalization: atomic per category. Used for board filtering and analytics. Example: Shown as section label in board list.
- `description`: Textual description of the category. Implements requirements for informative labeling. Example: 'Boards focused on regional and global market issues.' Normalization: atomic, nullable if not needed.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp for audit and traceability of board categories.

### `discussionboard_board_features`

Board feature flag entity - Implements the requirement for flexible configuration of board-level features (see: Core Functional Requirements, System Configuration, and Feature/Interaction Controls). 

Business explanation: Stores the enabled state of optional/experimental features on a per-board basis (e.g., can polls be posted, are reactions enabled, is anonymous posting allowed for this board?). Supports fine-grained feature rollout, A/B testing, or customized board behavior. Maintains 3NF: each feature assignment is atomic, attributes are not duplicated within board records.

Key relationships: Points to a board via foreign key. Used by admin/config UI. Referenced by runtime configuration code.
Special behaviors: Board id + feature_key must be unique; prevents duplicate assignments per board/feature.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for this specific feature flag assignment.
- `discussionboard_board_id`: Referenced board's [discussionboard_boards.id](#discussionboard_boards) - specifies which board's feature is being set.
- `feature_key`: Feature key string (e.g., 'enable_polls', 'anonymous_comments') - specifies which feature this record controls. Implements requirement for modular, extensible feature toggling. Example: Used to check board capabilities in code. Normalization: atomic and unique per board.
- `enabled`: Whether the feature is enabled on the associated board. Implements per-board feature flexibility and configuration management. Example: If false, UI disables poll creation for the board.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this feature flag was created. Implements audit and compliance requirements. For example, examining enabling/disabling of sensitive board features over time.

### `discussionboard_threads`

Discussion threads for the board - This implements requirements from 03_discussionboard_core_functional_requirements.md and 05_discussionboard_system_workflow_and_moderation_process.md. Provides the primary structure for aggregating posts and comments under a topic/theme. Maintains 3NF compliance: strictly stores only normalized data for the thread (no calculated fields). For example, a member creates a new thread, which is then referenced by posts and followed by others. Key relationships: referenced by follower and snapshot tables, and indirectly by discussionboard_posts, etc., in other domains. Special behaviors: Thread can be soft-deleted or archived, and supports search/tag/category relationships via references in other schemas.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `board_id`: Belonged board's [discussionboard_boards.id](#discussionboard_boards). Links thread to the parent board. Required for associating thread context and policy.
- `creator_member_id`: Creator's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). References the authoring member for auditing and permissions.
- `category_id`: Category's [discussionboard_board_categories.id](#discussionboard_board_categories). Associates thread with a board-level category for browsing and filtering.
- `title`: Title of the discussion thread - Implements the display and searchability requirements. Human-readable, indexed for search.
- `body`: Thread description or prompt - Implements content-rich initiation of discussion, markdown and media supported (but no storage here; attachments via relations).
- `status`: Thread status (e.g. 'active', 'archived', 'hidden', 'pending') - Supports workflow in moderation and visibility per business rules.
- `is_pinned`: Whether the thread is pinned to the top - Implements requirement for important conversations to be highlighted by moderators/admins.
- `is_locked`: Whether the thread is locked (no new posts/comments allowed) - Implements moderation/state transition requirement.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the thread was created - Fulfills audit and sorting requirements. Immutable after creation.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when thread metadata was last changed - Enables recency sorting, edit detection, and audit trail.
- `deleted_at`: When set, indicates the thread is soft-deleted (hidden from users but visible to mods/admins for audit and compliance) - Satisfies data retention policy. Null if not deleted.
- `archived_at`: When set, indicates the thread is archived (read-only, but not deleted). Implements post-lifecycle requirements for compliance/audit. Null if not archived.
- `last_activity_at`: Last activity timestamp - For thread sort order and engagement metrics. Not a calculated field; updated by triggers/actions.

### `discussionboard_thread_snapshots`

Thread snapshot entity - Implements audit and compliance requirements from 03_discussionboard_core_functional_requirements.md and 04_discussionboard_nonfunctional_and_policy_requirements.md. Stores normalized historical copies of thread metadata. Maintains 3NF by ensuring all data depends on the snapshot's unique identity, not introducing calculated fields. For example, when a thread's title or status changes, a new snapshot is recorded for traceability. Key relationship: Linked to the original thread; allows rollback/restore for legal or admin review. Special behaviors: Immutable once created.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `thread_id`: Target thread's [discussionboard_threads.id](#discussionboard_threads). Connects this snapshot to the original thread.
- `editor_member_id`: Editing member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Identifies the member who triggered the snapshot (edit, moderation, etc.).
- `title`: Thread title at snapshot time - Stores exact value of title as it was. Ensures 3NF; not duplicated beyond this time slice.
- `body`: Thread body at snapshot time - Captures thread description or prompt as it was before/after edit/mod. 3NF: Atomic per snapshot.
- `status`: Thread status at snapshot time (e.g., 'active', 'archived', etc.) - Enables changeset review for audit and compliance.
- `is_pinned`: Pinned flag at this snapshot - Allows forensic review of thread's highlighted state history.
- `is_locked`: Locked flag at this snapshot - Shows whether the thread was closed to comments/posts at this moment.
- `taken_at`: When this snapshot was captured - Timeline anchor for audit logs and rollback features.

### `discussionboard_thread_follows`

Entity tracking users following threads - Implements notification and engagement requirements from 03_discussionboard_core_functional_requirements.md. Strictly normalized: records each (follower, thread) pair with audit data but no aggregate/cached fields. For example, members follow threads to receive updates. Key relationships: references both member and thread tables; connected to notification mechanisms in another domain. Special behaviors: members cannot follow the same thread twice; soft-deletion allows for undos or compliance with erasure requests.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `thread_id`: Followed thread's [discussionboard_threads.id](#discussionboard_threads). Connects the follower to the thread.
- `member_id`: Follower's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Connects the action to a specific registered member.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when follow action was created - Fulfills audit and engagement analytics requirements. Atomic per action.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when follow action was undone (unfollowed or upon account/thread deletion). Implements right to erasure and compliance. Null if not deleted.

### `discussionboard_posts`

Discussion Post - Implements the main board content creation, visibility, and moderation requirements. Each row represents a user-created post, with atomic structure and all denormalized aspects such as comment count, like counts, and calculated metrics fully excluded as per 3NF normalization. Posts are linked by foreign keys to their authors and the thread they belong to, enabling complete audit trails and referential integrity.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `author_id`: Belonged member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). Identifies the author of the post, maintaining referential integrity to Actors domain.
- `thread_id`: Thread's [discussionboard_threads.id](#discussionboard_threads). Captures the thread which groups multiple posts as a single discussion timeline.
- `title`: Post title. Concise headline to describe the post subject.
- `body`: Rich-text/markdown body. Atomic representation of main post content.
- `is_published`: Publication state. True if public, false if draft or pending moderation.
- `published_at`: Timestamp of first publication, present only if published. Fulfills requirements for timeline and feed ordering.
- `deleted_at`: Soft-delete timestamp, nullable. Set when author/moderator requests deletion but content must remain for continuity/audit.
- `created_at`: Insertion/audit creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Atomic update timestamp. Set to latest edit, always enforced on atomic graphical or content edit.

### `discussionboard_post_edit_histories`

Post Edit History - Each edit of a post (by author, moderator, or admin) is recorded here as an atomic snapshot, fulfilling traceability and audit requirements for compliance and transparency. Designed as a historical log, fully normalized and versioned. No denormalized calculated data.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `post_id`: Target post's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts).
- `editor_id`: Responsible member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members). References member or moderator who made the change.
- `old_title`: Value before edit (title).
- `old_body`: Value before edit (body).
- `edit_reason`: Edit reason or policy justification note.
- `edited_at`: Timestamp of edit. Required for audit trails.

### `discussionboard_post_likes`

Post Likes - Each member liking a particular post has one atomic row per (member, post), enforcing single-like-per-user. Normalized so no aggregate counts are stored. Relates posts and members.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `post_id`: Target Post's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts).
- `member_id`: Liking member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members).
- `created_at`: Timestamp of like event.

### `discussionboard_post_dislikes`

Post Dislikes - Each member disliking a post creates a record per (member, post), preventing duplicate dislikes. Normalized; used for counting or abuse detection analytics outside this model.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `post_id`: Target post's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts).
- `member_id`: Disliking member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members).
- `created_at`: Timestamp of dislike event.

### `discussionboard_post_reports`

Post Reports - Every instance of a member reporting a post for policy violation, with all atomic details provided to ensure 3NF and normalization. Each row links reporter-member and post, and holds structured reason code and optional free-text evidence, as well as resolution tracking. No denormalized outcome/aggregate data is recorded here.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `post_id`: Target post's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts).
- `reporter_id`: Reporting member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members).
- `reason_code`: Reason code (enum/short string): e.g., 'spam', 'abuse', 'misinfo'.
- `reason_text`: Free text evidence or explanation. Optional.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp (audit).
- `resolved_at`: Moderator/admin action completion time. Null if unresolved.

### `discussionboard_post_attachments`

Post Attachments - Every asset attached to a post is referenced here. No BLOB/file data is stored, only file URIs and metadata. Enforces referential integrity to posts but does not link to users. Normalized structure only.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `post_id`: Post's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts).
- `file_uri`: Canonical URI/path to the file asset (may be internal or external repro).
- `file_name`: Original filename at upload.
- `mime_type`: File content-type, e.g., 'application/pdf', 'image/png'.
- `uploaded_at`: File timestamp at upload.

### `discussionboard_post_tags`

Post Tags - Junction table that maintains many-to-many relationship between posts and tags. Each row connects one post with one tag. Enforces unique constraint so tags cannot be duplicated per post. For tag information see Boards domain.

### `discussionboard_comments`

Discussion board comment entity - Implements comment-management and threading requirements from the platform RDD (incl. reply/nesting/audit). Each comment is tied to a post, a member (author), and optionally to another comment (for replies). Strict 3NF: all data is atomic, no duplication, all relations explicit. Used for creating, editing, replying, displaying, soft-deletion, and moderation/abuse tracing. Example: A member leaves a comment on a post, which may itself be a reply to another comment.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Serves as the unique identifier for the comment record.
- `discussionboard_post_id`: Parent post's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts) - Links this comment to the post under which it appears. Mandatory for proper placement in the post hierarchy.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Author's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) - References the member who authored the comment.
- `parent_id`: Parent comment's [discussionboard_comments.id](#discussionboard_comments) - Nullable for top-level comments. Enables threaded discussion structure.
- `body`: Comment text body. Contains the user-authored text or markdown submitted as the comment's main content. Example: 'I agree with your point, ...'
- `deleted`: Whether the comment is soft-deleted. Supports audit and discussion continuity by marking as deleted but retaining record. For example, deleted comments appear as 'This comment has been removed.'
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the comment was created. Indicates exact creation time and enables strict ordering.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the comment was last changed (edit, delete, restore, etc.). Used for edit windows, change history, and synchronization.

### `discussionboard_comment_edit_histories`

Comment edit history (snapshot) - Implements the audit logging requirement for comment edits. Each record represents a single edit to a comment, storing the full text as it existed at that edit. References both the comment and editor (in case moderator/staff performed correction). Strictly normalized: edits are not stored inline on main table, each edit is a new row. Enables audit trails, rollback, and viewing edit history, without denormalization.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussionboard_comment_id`: Target comment being edited.
- `edited_by_member_id`: Member who performed this edit (may differ from original author).
- `body`: Snapshot text of comment at time of this edit. Allows historical review and change tracking.
- `edited_at`: When the edit was made. Enables ordering of edit history and audit trail.

### `discussionboard_comment_likes`

Comment like action record. Corresponds to individual member's 'like' on a particular comment. Implements requirements for like/dislike granularity and auditability. Each like is its own row for normalization (not a counter). Uniqueness enforced for member+comment. Used for analytics, abuse prevention, reputation calculation. No aggregate/calculated fields in this table, only links and timestamp.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussionboard_comment_id`: The comment being liked (target).
- `discussionboard_member_id`: The member performing the like action.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when like was set. Used for analytics and audit.

### `discussionboard_comment_dislikes`

Dislike action record for comments. Fulfills requirement for member-level dislike tracking & abuse detection. Each record represents a member's single negative reaction to a comment; no aggregation/denormalization. Uniqueness constraint member+comment prevents duplicate dislikes. Strict normalization and audit compliance.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussionboard_comment_id`: The comment being disliked.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: The member performing the dislike action.
- `created_at`: When the dislike was set. Enables timeline analysis and audit.

### `discussionboard_comment_reports`

Comment report (flag) - Implements moderation and abuse workflow for individual comments. Records a member-generated report against a specific comment for review. Strictly normalized: can have multiple reports per member and comment (for various reasons/times). Supports compliance, anti-abuse, moderation tracing, and escalation. No aggregation/precalculation here. All moderator actions, resolutions, and workflows occur in moderation tables.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussionboard_comment_id`: The comment being reported.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: The member making this report.
- `reason_code`: Reason preset code (e.g., 'spam', 'harassment', 'copyright', etc). Controlled by content policy configuration, see moderation domain.
- `reason_details`: Detailed description (optional) entered by reporting member to explain or provide evidence. Only used for moderator context/notifying.
- `created_at`: When the report was created/submitted.

### `discussionboard_notifications`

Notification delivery record - This implements the notification delivery and tracking requirements from the requirements document (cf. notification mechanisms in core functional requirements and audit requirements). 

Business purpose: Keeps a persistent, queryable record of every notification (on-site, push, or email) sent to members concerning discussion board updates, replies, moderation outcomes, mentions, and critical policy changes. Ensures members can review notification history, supports audit/compliance logging, and allows for notification status management (delivered/read).

Normalization: 3NF compliant; notifications are only related to actual events (referenced by IDs), with no redundant/cached values. For example, a notification for a new moderator action would reference the related content without duplicating post/comment content here.

Key relationships: Will have a foreign key to discussionboard_members (member receiving the notification), and potentially to referenced entities (posts, comments, reports) via their IDs if required—those are soft-foreigns (UUIDs) to allow referencing dynamic business objects.

Special behaviors: Notifications are immutable records—once sent, status can only be updated (delivered/read), content doesn't change. Used for compliance/audit event trails.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies the notification delivery record.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: Target member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) who is receiving this notification. Ensures referential integrity between notification targets and registered users.
- `type`: Type of the notification (e.g., reply, mention, moderation_outcome, warning, policy_update, etc.). Implements requirement for notification categorization by event type. Ensures members can distinguish between notification classes. 3NF compliant by avoiding event duplication.
- `entity_type`: Kind of entity this notification references (e.g., post, comment, report, appeal, thread, policy). Implements requirement for referencing specific board objects related to the notification. Keeps this data atomic per 3NF.
- `entity_id`: ID of the business object this notification refers to (e.g., ID of a post, comment, report, etc.). Implements cross-entity traceability. Normalized: only contains object reference, not embedded content.
- `message`: Notification message shown to member (short body). Implements business requirement for delivering readable notification content. Normalization: message is tailored for notification but not duplicate of any business content.
- `delivered_at`: Timestamp when notification was delivered. 3NF: atomic business fact. Used for audit trail and delivery status UI.
- `read_at`: Timestamp when notification was marked as read by the member. Null if unread. Implements read-status tracking per user, normalized to this entity (not duplicated elsewhere).
- `channel`: Delivery channel (on_site, email, push, sms, etc). Implements requirement for specifying how notification was sent. Ensures UI can offer opt-out and channel-based filtering. Normalization: atomic value per record.

### `discussionboard_notification_preferences`

Notification preference settings for each member - This implements the requirement to allow members to configure how and for which events they receive notifications, as described in notification mechanism requirements.

Business purpose: Allows every member to store their notification preferences per notification type and channel (e.g., receive new reply notifications via on-site only, moderate actions by email, mentions by both, etc). Preferences drive notification delivery logic (e.g., block sending if opted out).

Normalization: 3NF compliance achieved by atomically storing each event type and channel in a preference row, rather than as a denormalized map or structure. For example, storing (member, type, channel, enabled) uniquely for every preference instead of an array keeps redundant data out.

Key relationships: Each record references the member (discussionboard_members table) whose preference is configured.

Special behaviors: Application logic ensures that on account deletion, all preferences are removed. Changes here directly affect notification sending at runtime.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies the preference row.
- `discussionboard_member_id`: [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) of the user whose preferences are being saved. Implements per-user notification customization, as required by the notification delivery and opt-out system. Maintains referential integrity with the member registry.
- `type`: Notification type this preference relates to (e.g., reply, mention, moderation_outcome, warning). Implements the event-based preference logic required. Atomic value per 3NF; ensures each row configures exactly one type.
- `channel`: The delivery channel for this preference ('on_site', 'email', 'push', etc). Implements the requirement for channel-based opt-out and customization. Atomic and 3NF normalized.
- `enabled`: Whether this member wants to receive this type of notification via this channel. Implements the opt-in/opt-out business requirement for notification personalization. No denormalized/cached flag map, 3NF compliant.

### `discussionboard_search_indexes`

Discussion board search index - This implements the search acceleration and full-text search requirement from the requirements document (see discussionboard_core_functional_requirements.md section 6: 'Search, Tagging, & Discovery').

Business purpose: Facilitates fast retrieval of posts, comments, and associated data for keyword and metadata-based searches, essential for performant user-facing discovery features. This table maintains a normalized, query-efficient structure for the inverted index or summary of searchable entities. Maintains 3NF compliance by separating search optimization data from the main content tables, with all index records strictly referencing the original content by unique identifiers. 

Usage example: Used when a user searches for keywords, tags, or authors; powers autocomplete, relevance scoring, and result ranking systems.

Key relationships: Reference to target entities such as posts, comments, threads (by their uuid), and tracking type. No foreign keys in this domain—relations are unidirectional from index towards existing business tables in other components. 

Special behaviors: Only core normalized index metadata is stored here—no computed ranking or denormalized result summaries allowed (those may be materialized in reporting views if necessary).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each search index record.
- `entity_id`: Target entity's [discussionboard_posts.id](#discussionboard_posts), [discussionboard_comments.id](#discussionboard_comments), or other content UUID depending on entity_type.
- `entity_type`: Type of entity referenced by this index record - Implements requirement for polymorphic search indexation (e.g., 'post', 'comment', 'thread'). Ensures normalization by recording only the primary entity type in atomic string format. For example, value 'post' for indexing a post content.
- `indexed_text`: Aggregated and normalized text used for full-text search - Combines title, body, and metadata fields in a canonical order for indexing. Implements core search requirements (requirement section 6). Stays fully normalized by representing only the atomic, canonical string. For example, concatenated post title and content, or comment body.
- `indexed_at`: Timestamp when this index entry was last generated/updated - Implements search freshness and incremental indexing needs. Maintains normalization by being a single timestamp per record. For example, updated whenever the associated entity changes.

### `discussionboard_search_histories`

Discussion board search histories - This implements the search analytics, audit, and user engagement/tracking requirements (see requirements 'audit & compliance logging' and 'search, tagging & discovery').

Business purpose: Records members' search actions, including terms searched and contextual metadata for system learning, personalization, and auditing. Maintains 3NF compliance by recording only normalized, atomic search event data. No aggregations or user-calculated fields present.

Usage example: Used for features like recent search re-surfacing, search analytics, and transparency/audit reporting.

Key relationships: Optionally references the member performing the search, and records search parameters and timestamps. No direct foreign keys in this table for loose coupling, but 'member_id' is provided as a reference for personalization/audit (references discussionboard_members.id).

Special behaviors: All data fully normalized; denormalized or aggregated reports must be built in separate materialized views.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each search history event.
- `member_id`: Reference to search-performing member's [discussionboard_members.id](#discussionboard_members) - Implements user-specific audit and personalization requirements. No enforced FK constraint for privacy and audit integrity.
- `search_terms`: Raw search query string(s) executed in this event - Implements the requirement for search auditing and analytics. Records the user's exact input, fully normalized as an atomic value per search event.
- `search_filters`: Serialized search filters or metadata (e.g., tags, date ranges) - Implements search capability analytics; records in atomic (normalized) format only, never as precomputed lists or aggregates. Example: JSON or CSV with filter parameters.
- `performed_at`: Timestamp when this search was performed - Required by audit, analytics, and for supporting 'recent searches' features. 3NF compliance: single value per row, no rollup.
- `result_count`: Number of results returned for this search event - Implements analytics requirement for search effectiveness, normalized with one row per search event. (May be used for user feedback and reporting.)

### `discussionboard_policies`

Platform Policy Record - Implements the core platform policy requirements, giving a canonical, versioned record for all operational and behavioral policy rules. Policy data is strictly normalized and auditable, directly mapping to documentation requirements and board policy enforcement. Example: 'Community Guidelines v2.3' issued on a specific date. Integrates with audit logs and is referenced for compliance and moderator review. Only most recent is currently enforced, older remain for trace/audit.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each discussion board policy record.
- `title`: Policy title, e.g. 'Community Guidelines' or 'Content Moderation Policy'. Maintains normalization, avoids duplication. Implements document clarity.
- `body`: Full text body of the policy, in markdown or rich text. Implements requirement for accessible, canonical platform policy. For example, the text visible to all members or in legal export. Fully normalized: not duplicated in reports/notifications.
- `version`: Version or revision string, e.g. 'v2.3'. Tracks updates and historic changes. Enables transparent history/audit. Example: used for date-based policy lookup or regulatory export.
- `effective_at`: The date/time when the policy comes into effect. Enables lifecycle and audit tracing. Null when not yet active or for drafts. For example: a policy published for enforcement starting next month.
- `expired_at`: When a policy is superseded or withdrawn. Null if still current. Ensures that only one policy is enforced at a time and supports regulatory retention requirements.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of policy creation. Satisfies requirements for audit logging.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last update. Ensures audit and policy lifecycle are tracked.
- `created_by`: UUID of the member/moderator/admin who created this policy. Supports audit reporting, foreign key to actors table (exists in other component). Does not duplicate actor data.

### `discussionboard_policy_updates`

Policy Update/Event Log - Implements transparent policy change and notification history. Records all updates to policies, enabling complete audit/compliance trail. Mapped directly to board transparency, legal, and user-notification requirements. Allows admins/moderators/members to see what was changed, when, and by whom. Enforces 3NF by separating update events/actors from the policy content itself.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each policy update record.
- `discussionboard_policy_id`: Target policy being updated. References [discussionboard_policies.id](#discussionboard_policies), supporting referential integrity. Key in policy-update history. Maintains normalization in event/audit trails.
- `actor_id`: Actor (admin/moderator/member) making the update (references IDs from respective actors tables—already defined in other components). Normalized and used for audit reporting, does not duplicate actor data.
- `change_summary`: Summary description of what changed and why (for transparency and audit); e.g., 'Clarified spam definition; updated reporting workflow.' 3NF compliance: not embedded in policy or notification structures.
- `created_at`: Event creation timestamp. Satisfies need for sequenced, auditable event logs.

### `discussionboard_community_guidelines`

Community Guidelines Canonical Record - Fulfills the need for a canonical, structured storage of community guidelines, versioned with independent lifecycle tracking. Integrates with moderation and onboarding functions. Ensures canonical, up-to-date guidelines are referenceable without duplication. Only currently effective guideline is visible to members; previous versions are preserved for legal and compliance review.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Unique identifier for community guidelines.
- `title`: Guideline section or doc title, e.g. 'Acceptable Use', 'Prohibited Behavior'. Atomic/normalized for search/display.
- `body`: Full guideline content, markdown allowed. Canonical, structural, normalized; covers the specific rules detailed for users/moderators/auditors.
- `version`: Version/revision tag, e.g. 'v2.0', '2025-07'. Enables traceable guideline life cycle. Normalized: not duplicated in child records.
- `effective_at`: When this guideline text becomes authoritative. Enables future-dated guideline publication. Null for not-in-force or draft entries.
- `expired_at`: When this version is retired/superseded; null if active. Enforces policy history/lifecycle business rules.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when guideline section is created. Audit log compliance and historical integrity.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last change to guideline text. Complete update/audit trail. 3NF: kept atomic to avoid duplicate history.
- `created_by`: UUID of creating admin or member (references ID in actors component). Enables history/audit trace, no actor info duplication.

Permissions may restrict some results for non-admin roles. The API incorporates sorting and advanced search, and will be used by admins, moderators, and members to discover channels. Error responses will provide validation, permission, and query failure details. Pagination uses standard page/size parameters, enabling large-scale enumeration without performance penalty.

The id path parameter corresponds to the primary UUID key of the discussionboard_channels Prisma table. Used for displaying channel detail views in user interfaces, and for management tasks by admins or moderators. Permission rules restrict access to hidden or soft-deleted channels for some roles. Errors will be returned for invalid ids or insufficient permissions.

operations.specification: Create a new system configuration entry in discussionboard_configurations. This operation allows authorized administrators to add a new platform-wide configuration parameter for the discussion board application, such as toggling maintenance mode, configuring global limits, or changing policy strings. The payload specifies the atomic config_key, config_value (as string), value_type (such as boolean/int/string/datetime), and optional description. Creation and update timestamps are managed automatically. All configuration parameters must be unique by config_key and are strictly enforced at the database level. This endpoint is essential for DevOps and admin panel integration to handle runtime and policy settings. Only platform administrators are authorized to perform this operation.
operations.description: This operation creates a new system configuration entry in discussionboard_configurations. The body must include config_key (string), config_value (string), value_type (string, like 'boolean'/'int'/'string'/'datetime'), and an optional description. Upon creation, system-managed timestamps are recorded. Only admins may invoke this endpoint. Attempts to duplicate config_key will result in an error; config keys are unique and required for mapping application configuration at runtime. All system, security, and audit logging for configuration events should be consulted in tandem for compliance. Authorization token is required.
operations.summary: Create a new configuration in discussionboard_configurations.

requestBody.description: Configuration creation details. Must include: config_key, config_value, value_type, and optional description.

responseBody.description: The created configuration entry details in the system.

operations.specification: Update an existing configuration entry identified by its UUID in discussionboard_configurations. This enables modification of system-wide operational or policy configuration parameters, adhering to platform audit and compliance requirements. Configuration modifications require strict validation: only the config_value, value_type, and description can be updated. The config_key and id are immutable; creation timestamp never changes, but updated_at is set to the time of modification. The endpoint enforces unique constraints and proper atomicity of configuration parameters. Only platform administrators have modify permission. Use for admin UI configuration change features and runtime system tuning.
operations.description: This operation updates an existing configuration in discussionboard_configurations by UUID. Accepts input for config_value, value_type, and description; config_key and id are immutable and cannot be changed. Authorization is required and only admins are permitted access. Attempts to update non-existent configurations will return a 404 error. Audit log entries should record the update. Unique constraints are validated on the config_key, and all updates record updated_at timestamp for compliance.
operations.summary: Update an existing configuration in discussionboard_configurations.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Target configuration's UUID.

requestBody.description: Config update information: value, type, description (cannot update id or config_key).

responseBody.description: The updated configuration entry.

operations.specification: Remove a configuration entry (soft-delete) from discussionboard_configurations by UUID. This operation marks the configuration as deleted for compliance and audit; actual record remains for historical reference. Only system administrators have the authority to delete configurations. Invoking this endpoint updates the record's soft-delete field (not a hard delete), allowing potential restoration and complete audit trails for past system settings. Used in admin UIs and DevOps workflows when a configuration becomes obsolete or policy changes.
operations.description: This endpoint marks a configuration in discussionboard_configurations as deleted (soft-deletion) using its UUID. Soft-deletion ensures the database retains the record for compliance and auditing but removes it from active configuration loads. Authorization is restricted to system admins. If the ID does not exist, a 404 error is returned. All deletions must be logged in the system audit log. Attempts to delete a configuration that is already deleted will have no side effect beyond idempotent compliance logging.
operations.summary: Soft-delete a configuration in discussionboard_configurations.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Target configuration's UUID to delete.

responseBody.description: No content. Indicates soft-deletion was successful or already completed.

operations.specification: Retrieve a paginated, searchable list of audit logs from discussionboard_audit_logs for compliance reviews. This endpoint is crucial for administrators to monitor and inspect policy-critical or sensitive actions throughout the system (e.g., configuration changes, moderation actions, user escalation events). Supports search/filtering by actor_id, action_type, action_scope, target_id, and timestamp ranges. The PATCH method allows a complex request body for filtering instead of relying on query parameters, supporting advanced search cases. All returned data is read-only and for review/reporting purposes—no sensitive information is redacted for authorized roles. Authorization: admin only.
operations.description: Returns a paginated, filtered list of audit log entries from discussionboard_audit_logs. Accepts advanced search criteria including actor_id, action_type, action_scope, target_id, and time range. Useful for compliance and post-incident analysis. Result includes metadata required for pagination and auditing. Access limited to admins; audit logs are read-only and retained permanently for regulatory compliance.

All associated business object references are provided for context—real entity records may need to be queried separately. Authorization restricted to admins and platform compliance auditors.
operations.description: Gets a single audit log entry from discussionboard_audit_logs by its UUID. Full record of the action, actor, target, scope, and all metadata is included. The endpoint ensures all compliance/audit logging data can be promptly reviewed by authorized personnel only. If entry is not found, returns 404.
